# flutter_constraint_layout

> A faithful port of Android ConstraintLayout to Flutter, in pure Dart. Every child is a direct child of one `ConstraintLayout`, and each child declares where its edges go (pinned to the parent or to a sibling by id) and how it is sized. The widget tree stays flat instead of nesting rows, columns, and stacks, and the same layout runs on iOS, Android, web, macOS, Windows, and Linux.

flutter_constraint_layout is pure Dart (no native code, no platform setup) and runs on every Flutter platform. Add it with `flutter pub add flutter_constraint_layout` (or `flutter_constraint_layout: ^1.0.0` under `dependencies` in `pubspec.yaml`) and import `package:flutter_constraint_layout/flutter_constraint_layout.dart`, which brings in every widget, dimension, link, and helper. It requires Dart 3.12 or newer and Flutter 3.44 or newer, and its API is designed around Dart dot shorthands. Children are declared with the `Constrained` widget, each keyed by a `Symbol` id, and positioned with dot-shorthand constraints such as `.startOf(parent, margin: 16)`, `.fixed(56)`, `.matchConstraint`, `.percent(0.5)`, `.spread`, `.packed`, and `.gone`. Helpers like `Guideline` and `Barrier`, chains, aspect ratios, circular positioning, and the virtual `ConstraintFlow` and `ConstraintGrid` layouts cover the arrangements that usually require extra wrapper widgets. Under the hood a deterministic dependency-graph resolver handles most layouts and falls back to a slower Cassowary constraint solver for the rest, such as a layout with a barrier, a circular link, a `ConstraintFlow` or `ConstraintGrid`, or a chain with a gone or aspect-ratio member. The engine is a line-faithful port of androidx constraintlayout core whose resolver is verified at parity with core 1.1.1.

**Read the docs first.** The Markdown file below is the website's docs page in one file (installation, anchoring edges, right-to-left rules, bias and centering, constraint dimensions, aspect ratios, chains, guidelines, barriers, circular positioning, visibility and gone, the virtual Flow and Grid layouts, a worked example, and the engine internals). Fetch it before answering questions about this package: it is compact Markdown written to be read in one pass. It is a guided tour, not the full reference: the package README, listed after it, is the full guide and also covers z-order, sizing inside scroll views and intrinsic sizing, the debug overlay, unknown and duplicate ids, common mistakes, performance, and the limitations and differences from Android.

**Build each `Symbol` id the same way everywhere.** A literal id such as `#avatar` is fine when every link and `referenced` entry also uses the literal. For ids made in a loop with `Symbol('item$i')`, refer to them only through the same call, for example a helper `Symbol item(int i) => Symbol('item$i');`, never through a literal such as `#item0` or a `const Symbol('item0')`. Release and profile WebAssembly builds, and builds compiled with `--obfuscate`, rename symbol literals, so there `#item0` is not equal to `Symbol('item0')` and a link that mixes the two forms is silently skipped, even though it works in debug builds.

## Docs

- [flutter_constraint_layout documentation (Markdown)](https://constraints.birju.dev/docs.md): The entire docs page as one Markdown file. Fetch and read this in full for accurate API usage, constraint syntax, code examples, and layout patterns; prefer it over guessing.
- [Package README (full guide)](https://github.com/BirjuVachhani/flutter_constraint_layout/blob/main/packages/flutter_constraint_layout/README.md): The complete user guide, also shown on pub.dev: every link, dimension, and helper option, z-order, right-to-left rules, sizing and scrolling, the debug overlay, unknown and duplicate ids, common mistakes, performance, and the limitations and differences from Android. Read it for anything the docs page does not cover.

## Reference

- [Package on pub.dev](https://pub.dev/packages/flutter_constraint_layout): Versions, API reference, and install instructions.
- [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/BirjuVachhani/flutter_constraint_layout): Repository, issues, and changelog.
- [Live documentation site](https://constraints.birju.dev/docs): The interactive docs, with every example rendered live beside its code.

## Optional

- [flutter_constraint_layout_lints](https://github.com/BirjuVachhani/flutter_constraint_layout/tree/main/packages/flutter_constraint_layout_lints): An analyzer plugin that warns about duplicate and undefined constraint ids (`duplicate_constraint_id`, `undefined_constraint_id`).
- [constraint_engine](https://github.com/BirjuVachhani/flutter_constraint_layout/tree/main/packages/constraint_engine): The pure-Dart layout engine underneath, with no Flutter dependency.
- [Android ConstraintLayout (upstream)](https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/views/layout/constraint-layout): The original Android layout this package ports. Its constraint concepts carry over; MotionLayout, `ConstraintSet`, `Group`, `Layer`, and `Placeholder` are not ported, and the package README lists the remaining differences.
- [androidx constraintlayout core](https://github.com/androidx/constraintlayout): The Java source the layout engine is ported from.
